report.source_text: A two-year-old boy presented at the emergency department for an extremely painful bilateral non-pitting edema of both hands (Fig. 1). No fever neither trauma occurred. At examination, the child was well, but he could not use his hands nor walked. Purpuric lesions on the left cheek, nostril and ear were noted (Fig. 2).

report.source_text: Our patient received treatment with ibuprofen. Lesions resolved in 72 h.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A two-year-old boy presented with painful bilateral non-pitting edema of the hands and purpuric lesions on the face without fever or trauma (E001). Laboratory tests showed normal blood cell count, elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 14.2 mg/dL, ESR 110 mm/hr), and negative urinalysis (E002). During observation, edema and purpuric lesions spread to arms, feet, and legs (E003). Skin biopsy was ordered but histopathology results were not documented. The patient was treated with ibuprofen and lesions resolved within 72 hours (E005).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation of painful bilateral hand edema and purpuric lesions on face in a well-appearing child without fever or trauma
Laboratory findings of normal blood count, elevated CRP and ESR, negative urinalysis indicating inflammation without systemic infection
Progression of edema and purpura to other extremities during observation
Resolution of lesions after treatment with ibuprofen in 72 hours

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: No fever or systemic signs, negative urinalysis, and spontaneous resolution after symptomatic treatment
Laboratory tests normal aside from inflammatory markers; biopsy not available but clinical course typical of acute hemorrhagic edema

remaining_uncertainties: Histopathological confirmation of leukocytoclastic vasculitis from skin biopsy was not documented
